title: Completion widget not keyboard navigable
body:
Ref #173622

Assuming we could fix the ghost text issue and give screen readers users a hint how to open the widget—if that's the right thing to do—it looks like we could then continue on to ensure that the tooltip is reading more than just the current suggestion.

From what I can tell, it isn't possible to use the keyboard to navigate through the widget actions. Is there a way to arrow through these without dismissing it? Could we put focus on the first enabled button when it pops up? There may be other ways. Just getting the conversation started.

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/25163139/217103076-924e2dbc-95b1-4529-830a-5b527155f854.mp4

cc @isidorn @hediet @esonnino @meganrogge

similar_issues.text: No indication of ghost text and actions via screen reader. as far as i can tell, we blow right by the ghost text if displayed — i only hear the next visible line being read. i expected to hear the suggestion read out, and then ideally get some sort of access to the hover widget via the keyboard. do we have any precedent for having the screen reader output something like " press [ inline _ code ] for more suggestions and actions "? https : / / user - images. githubusercontent. com / 25163139 / 217100999 - da3b2ef9 - f8b7 - 4449 - 802e - d63311537b5a. mp4 cc @ isidorn @ hediet @ esonnino @ meganrogge

Don't close suggest widget when cycling with tab completion. i really like the [ inline _ code ] setting, but as soon as i insert a suggestion the suggest widget closes and i am no longer able to see the suggestions i am cycling through while pressing [ inline _ code ]. i would expect the suggest widget to stay open, mainly because i consider the concept of tab completion as indifferent to the presence of the widget. when i turn [ inline _ code ] on and from then on the widget disappears as soon i am choosing what to insert, this kind of feels like a surprising side effect. i would prefer the widget to stay open as long as i am cycling through suggestions, close / refresh it with the next non - tab keystroke and therefore have it open as long as i am using tab completion. this way i instantly see how often i have to press tab until i reach the suggestion i want to insert. therefore i suggest an additional option to keep the widget open when using tab completion. also i guess this is what # 59828 was actually about, but i don't use xcode, so i am not 100 % sure.

UI - Improve the suggest widget performance. * * issue : * * # 1923 * * assignees : * * - [ x ] windows @ gregvanl - [ x ] os x @ isidorn - [ x ] linux @ aeschli * * details : * * the suggest widget underwent a big refactoring. it is now implemented using a new list widget for better performance. please stress test it with all of its use cases. - keyboard navigation - mouse navigation - large list of suggestions ( over 20k ). you can use joh's [ brutalo extension ] ( https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode / files / 108309 / language - brutalo. zip ).

Keyboard accessibility and focus indication. - [ x ] win @ alexandrudima - [ x ] mac @ joaomoreno - [ x ] linux @ isidorn we no longer hide the focus outline when using the [ inline _ code ] key to move focus into an element in the dom. we added more support for using [ inline _ code ] and [ inline _ code ] keys to navigate between ui controls in the workbench and editor. * * note * * : enable accessibility mode in the editor to be able to tab out of it ( [ inline _ code ] ) * * note * * : you might end up in a situation where you do not see any focus indication. open the console and type [ inline _ code ] to find out where you are currently at and file a bug if you think something is wrong. - verify you can use [ inline _ code ] to jump to ui controls and you get meaningful focus indication - verify you can use the [ inline _ code ] keys in ui control groups to jump between controls ( e. g. in action bars ) - verify you never end up in a situation where you can not continue to tab out of a control

Suggest accessibility: make announcements more concise. we got feedback from users for debug accessibility to make the announcements as concise as possible. here are some ideas on how to make it more concise for suggest widget : 1. do not announce'suggestion'after each suggestion, instead of that announce when suggest widget opened and closed - that way the user will know that what he is hearing are suggestions inside the widget 2. instead of saying'name, suggestion accepted'just say'name, accepted'@ zersiax opinions very welcome

title: Auto synchronize user extensions with remote hosts
body:
I know that I can already use this little button:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/29582865/218273235-1ba21cba-3fc4-4f6c-8f5f-250f775b083a.png)

To install all my extensions in a remote target. But:

- I often forget about it, as this is a manual step
- I install extensions in some other computers, which gets synchronized to my main computer, but not to my remote target

Some of us uses remote hosts as if they were our main dev rig, like WSL for example.

I think it would be great if there was a way to opt-in for an **auto synchronize user extensions** with remote hosts.

And by synchronize, I mean both automatically installing and uninstalling, because why not?

similar_issues.text: Sync remote extensions when turning on Sync. also sync remote extensions ( wsl, ssh, dev container ) while syncing

no way to not sync newly installed Extensions by default. if the settings sync is on ( with extensions sync there ), the newly installed extensions get synced by default, and there is no way to change it. that is, the " sync this extension " tick is always on by default :! [ image ] ( https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode / assets / 233979 / b0991aef - 45fe - 4c4e - 9858 - 4dc483fa6810 ) while it might be not desired behavior per se, it also creates additional problems as : - if extension pack is being installed ( as on the screenshot ), even if we disable the " sync this extension " tick before - all the extensions it includes will be synced upon the installation. - even if we manually disable every newly installed extension from syncing after, one by one - they might be already synchronized at the moment, and keep be installed remotely after we managed to disable their sync. as a solution, there should be an option to keep the " sync this extension " tick off by default. does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled? : yes - vs code version : version : 1. 85. 1 - os version : browser : mozilla / 5. 0 ( x11 ; ubuntu ; linux x86 _ 64 ; rv : 121. 0 ) gecko / 20100101 firefox / 121. 0 steps to reproduce : 1. make sure the settings sync is on 2. open settings context menu of any new extension, as on the screenshot 3. note the " sync this extension " tick is always set by default @ sandy081

Provide support to synchronize settings across machines. there are quiet some extensions out there to handle setting synchronization between multiple computers. and in my opinion they are very important : since vscode is very customizable with settings, keyboardshortcuts and extension it is very hard to synchronize those things between multiple workstations. and all those extensions are not really clean solutions, because vscode does nearly nothing to support them ( for example the paths vscode uses are not exposed, see # 2741 ). so here some ideas to make synchronization clean and extensible : - add a contribution point for synchronization extensions - those extensions should not have to gather all the files that have to be synced. vscode should do this and then pass them to the extensions - such an extension's job is only to upload / download the files, passed to them ( so we can have the [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ] / [ inline _ code ]. - or maybe gather all settings into one big json object and pass that. - support versioning and non versioning extensions - add a remote _ settings. json to build on top of the workspace - settings / user - settings stack. - allow automatic and user triggered synchronization ok... just some ideas : smile :

Feature Request: A native solution to sync user settings. rather than using an extension, i'd like a way to be able to login to vscode so that i can sync my user settings, extensions, code snippets, etc from machine to machine. kind of like logging into google chrome

Syncing uninstallation of extension doesn't appear to work. originally posted by @ tylerleonhardt it seems to be very hard to properly uninstall an extension because of settings sync and the 1 - many relationship of codespaces. i have a my local dev env, and then a few codespaces. if i try uninstalling an extension in my local dev env and then move over to my codespace, it still has the extension installed and it appeared to sync it back and then it was back on my local dev env. i've had to uninstall the same extension numerous times. steps to repro : 1. start a couple codespaces 2. close out of your codespaces 3. open vscode local and install an extension ( it works best if it's an extension pack like : https : / / marketplace. visualstudio. com / items? itemname = docsmsft. docs - authoring - pack ) 4. open the codespaces and verify the sync happened on the remote side 5. close all codespaces tabs ( but don't destroy them ) 6. uninstall the docs authoring pack locally 7. log in to your codespaces and wait a bit... you should still see the docs authoring pack 8. uninstall the docs authoring pack in the codespaces 9. close the codespaces 10. check local and then also reopen the codespaces you should see the docs authoring pack still installed in codespaces

title: Add category function for installed Extensions
body:
Given the large number of Extensions (100+) that users may install. Some of these Extensions may be serving the c++ workspace and some the python workspace.

title: [Accessibility] Line-by-line audio cues are not played when column position is away from the event trigger spot
body:
CC @meganrogge

## Reproducible Steps

1. Load screen reader.

1. Open the following in code-insiders mode: https://github.dev/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/README.md

1. Press Ctrl+G (go to line) and type [INLINE_CODE] and hit enter.

1. While keeping the column position at 9, move lines by pressing UpArrow and DownArrow and come back to line 64: audio cue is not played.

1. This time, place your cursor to the left ([INLINE_CODE]) and do the same thing as above: audio cue is now played.

## Current Behavior

1. Line 64 has a warning and the audio cue is not played when you press UpArrow/DownArrow and come back to this line.

## Expected Beaavior

Audio cues should be played when UpArrow/DownArrow is used.

## System Info

Version: 1.76.0-insider (system setup)
Commit: 78cb4eb690930964f4dcddde7c4828bdb5beaabd
Date: 2023-02-20T11:45:27.892Z
Electron: 19.1.10
Chromium: 102.0.5005.196
Node.js: 16.14.2
V8: 10.2.154.26-electron.0
OS: Windows_NT x64 10.0.22621
Sandboxed: Yes

similar_issues.text: Refine error on line audio cue. screen reader users navigate through an editor via the arrow keys / mouse and are informed of errors with an audio cue when : 1. the cursor lands on a line with an error via line change 3. the cursor lands in an error range via a column change when a screen reader user goes to a new line with an error, they hear the audio cue, but aren't advised as to whether or not the column they've landed on contains an error. in order to know this, they must explore the characters on that line. while working on the fix for https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode / issues / 174857, @ kieferrm suggested it could be advantageous to have separate audio cues for each context. that would fix this case. here's what i propose : separate audio cues for : 1. the cursor lands within an error range via line and / or column change 2. the cursor lands on a line with an error outside of the error range via line change any thoughts are appreciated : @ isidorn and @ jooyoungseo

refine when accessibility signals play in code editor. type : < b > bug < / b > i'm grouping together in this single issue several issues related to audio cues and accessibility - related text notifications in the editor. this is because they appear to be closely related and likely share a common cause. it is suspected that the triggering mechanism for both the audio cue and the text alert is the same, leading to the observed problematic behavior. in the visual studio code editor, there are issues related to the audio cues that have been present in previous versions. additionally, with the introduction of accessibility - related text notifications in v1. 86, new problems have arisen. these notifications, intended for screen reader users, are triggered when the cursor encounters lines with errors, warnings, breakpoints, etc. the issues with these features are as follows : 1. both the audio cues and accessibility - related text notifications are triggered whenever the cursor moves within the line, such as when using control + left / right to navigate to the previous / next word. this is particularly disruptive for the text notifications, as the repeated reading of the word " error ", " warning ", etc., often interrupts the normal verbalization of the screen reader. it would be more effective if these cues and notifications were only triggered when moving to a different line. 2. there appears to be a slight delay before the accessibility - related notification is announced. if the user moves too quickly between lines, the notification is not read in sync with the corresponding line, or sometimes it is read multiple times. it would be more efficient if the notification for a line was cancelled when the user moves to another line, ensuring it is always synchronized with the appropriate line. an advanced approach could be to have different audio cues for line - specific errors / warnings / breakpoints and " inline " errors / warnings / breakpoints. one suggestion would be to use the same sound but with different pitches for these two types of cues. this would not be necessary for certain audio cues that are only line - specific ( such as folded code ) or triggered by specific events ( such as task audio cues ). vs code version : code 1. 86. 0 ( 05047486b6df5eb8d44b2ecd70ea3bdf775fd937, 2024 - 01 - 31t10 : 28 : 19. 990z ) os version : windows _ nt x64 10. 0.

Column select does not behave intuitively or consistently with other common editors. this reproduces on all platforms and all versions of vscode. 1. enter three lines of text : [ code _ block ] 2. use column - select to select bcd from the middle and press ctrl + x to cut it. 3. place the cursor after the c on the first line and make sure to you're out of multi - cursor edit mode. 4. press ctrl + v the end result is this : [ code _ block ] the result should be this : [ code _ block ] now, * * if * * you re - enter multi - cursor mode and select a 0x3 region on the right and then paste, it works. but this is both impractical * and * inconsistent with other editors. it is impractical because for a large region of text, one can't realistically remember how many columns were selected as part of the cut / copy operation, and re - selecting a region of exactly the same size on the paste is basically impossible. if you plan to paste within the same file, you might get lucky and have this work ( as long as you don't click the mouse anywhere else at all before you go to the area you want to paste into ), but if you want to paste into a separate editor window there's no solution here, because the editor forgets how many columns were selected as part of the original multi - cursor copy / cut operation. it also means that if i cut from vscode and paste into another editor ( or vice versa ), it won't work correctly. it is inconsistent with other editors because visual studio proper, notepad + +, and many other editors behave the way i've described as " expected " up above. if you do a box select and then copy or cut, then move the cursor anywhere else in the file ( or another file ) and paste, it behaves as expected. it appears that vscode is buggy on * both * the copy as well as the paste operations. i determined that copy is buggy in vscode by first selecting a rectangular area in notepad + + and pasting it into visual studio ( not vscode ). it behaves as expected, suggesting that this information is retained even cross - process, and that as long as clipboard data is constructed properly, visual studio can correctly paste data that was copied from another program. but

screenreader reading of inline errors. issue type : < b > feature request < / b > # feature description we already have audio queues for when the focus goes over a line that contains errors, perhaps to give us the same experience sighted people have, where they see the errors underlined in red i believe. next step, the same way sighted people can mouse over the portion of code underlined in red to see a tool - tip with the error message, we should also get the same information either by explicitly pressing a key, or through the mechanism that's already used for parameter hints # how should it work? 1. open a file in vscode, the language should be detectable and an extension that provides the language server should be installed 2. if there isn't any error, make one 3. with the arrow keys, go over that line. if everything is working right, you should hear the tone meant for errors now, you could either wait a bit longer while on that line to hear the error text if using the parameter hint mechanism, or press a key command to do the same thing if you think the params hint way is too noisy and you want the users to have explicit control over when the screen - reader reads the error content. yes, i know i could use the problems view, but sometimes i have so many errors and warnings from other files as well, that the error i'm literally focused on is lost in the noise. i could also use the mouse over command, but that only works as long as my cursor is focused on the part of the line where the underlining in red begins. since i don't have any way to know where that is, i can't use that feature as it is. furthermore, the mouse over command pops up a tool - tip which moves the focus of the screen reader, requiring me to press the escape key to get back to the editor, so going through the problems view or issuing the next / previous problem commands would end up being more efficient. # environment information vs code version : code 1. 66. 2 ( dfd34e8260c270da74b5c2d86d61aee4b6d56977, 2022 - 04 - 11t07 : 46 : 01. 075z ) os version : windows _ nt x64 10. 0. 19044 restricted mode : no

Screen reading. * * issue : * * # 3058 * * assignees : * * - [ x ] windows @ stevencl - [ x ] windows @ weinand * * details : * * - download and install or simply run once ( there is away to run without installing ) nvda from http : / / www. nvaccess. org / - if you want to avoid hearing it : right click on the tray icon and choose tools > speech viewer. optionally stop the voice via tray icon and preferences > synthesizer > no speech - edit your settings ( user or workspace ) and set [ inline _ code ]. - validate the setting is turned on by going to an editor and pressing [ inline _ code ] * * learn basic nvda operations * * - tray icon > help > commands quick reference - afaik nvda works in different modes and you need to be aware in what mode you are : - using [ inline _ code ] and cursor keys to navigate is ok, but you should be aware and perhaps try out other navigation options. - nvda has another conceptual " review cursor " besides the normal one ( e. g. allows for reading other parts of text without moving the editor cursor ) - when in one of the browse modes, it is possible that keypresses are eaten up by nvda for navigation purposes, so you should at least at a minimum understand that there are these modes and that you switch between them, - toggle browse / focus modes [ inline _ code ] - review modes : next via [ inline _ code ], prev via [ inline _ code ]. - look at commands in the object navigation section, they allow to navigate the accessibility tree. - look at commands in the reviewing text section : e. g. move to previous word ( [ inline _ code ] ), report current word ( [ inline _ code ] ), move to next word ( [ inline _ code ] ), move to previous character ( [ inline _ code ] ), report current character ( [ inline _ code ] ), move to next character ( [ inline _ code ] ). - i am not sure what commands are most important or most used. * * try to do a programming task such as fix a bug * * - we want to also discover what is not screen reader accessible, but also validate what we have done explicitly : - title: Explorer: limit auto-expansion of workspace roots when number is large
body:
I was browsing a workspace of 1000 folders and the window got stuck trying to expand all of them on startup. Maybe we can limit this to reduce pressure, i.e. when I open a workspace, only expand all roots when there are not more than 10 roots or 20.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/900690/223179810-5f0497b2-b88a-40ad-8e73-6c5de82aed29.png)

similar_issues.text: File explorer is expanding all root folders in a MR workspace. steps to reproduce : 1. create a mr workspace file with more than one folder 2. open the mr workspace all top level folders are expanded. this is very slow if there are lot of root folders and also if the mr workspace is in remote

Allow to set explorer.autoReveal per specific folder. issue type : < b > feature request < / b > node _ modules will constantly expand itself in the explorer, especially if your defining definitions. i typically never want this, i think an exception should be made for showing what file is open if its in node _ modules to keep the folder collapsed unless i explicitly expand it. the reason it's a problem is because there are so many files in node _ modules you have to collapse it to keep developing, as it's completely useless in most cases to have it expanded and it pushes your work files off screen. proposition : - never expand node _ modules implicitly - if goto definition is used into a node _ module, go there but do not older current folder state ( if its collapsed keep it collapsed, if it was explicitly expanded by user keep it ). - this behavior applies very specifically to node _ modules only. vs code version : code - insiders 1. 42. 0 - insider ( 7c0095ee2d064033fc13184127a9adc603454729, 2019 - 12 - 20t07 : 58 : 23. 119z ) os version : linux x64 5. 3. 0 - 24 - generic

Have a setting for maximum number open files (editors). i've noticed that there is no way to limit the number of total files open at once. there is an [ inline _ code ] option, but that seems to limit the height of the " open editors " pane ( which i don't use - i use tabs instead ). to keep my workspace focused, i like my editor to automatically close files over a set threshold that i have least recently viewed. obviously, it wouldn't close files that have unsaved changes ( or it would prompt you prior to trying to close them ). does this sound like a reasonable request? please let me know!

Expand all subfolders in Explorer view. type : < b > feature request < / b > hi, i found myself wanting to list all files and folders insdie a project in explorer view to get a birds - eye view of the structure of the project. the " collapse " button is available, but there is no such thing as an expand button on a folder or root folder which i think might be missing. thank you. vs code version : code 1. 95. 3 ( f1a4fb101478ce6ec82fe9627c43efbf9e98c813, 2024 - 11 - 13t14 : 50 : 04. 152z ) os version : windows _ nt x64 10. 0. 26100 modes : remote os version : linux x64 5. 15. 0 - 130 - generic remote os version : linux x64 5. 15. 0 - 130 - generic remote os version : linux x64 5. 15. 0 - 130 - generic

Ability to enable extensions only on specific workspaces. # 2882 recently added the ability to disable extensions either globally or on specific workspaces. with these new options, it is now possible to have extensions enabled on all except some selected workspaces. however, it currently does not seem to be possible to enable extensions on specific workspaces while disabling them on all others, effectively the inverse of what is currently implemented. i am currently running some extensions that incorrectly activate on workspaces they should not, and there is no way around it apart from toggling the enabled / disabled state every time i open a workspace < sup > 1 < / sup >. this is a rather tedious process. getting the extension author to leave a marker file also pollutes the workspace, and some extension authors may not be willing to do so. - - - < sup > < sup > 1 < / sup > disabling them on each workspace manually isn't a great solution, when i often use " open with code " on previously - unvisited directories. this particular offending extension ends up creating a hidden settings folder, leaving them scattered around unrelated directories. < / sup >

title: Pin editor keyboard shortcut sometimes doesn't work
body:
Type: Bug This started happening since the latest patch. One way I was able to reproduce: There is more than one editor open. At least one editor is pinned. There is only one editor that is not pinned. For that one editor that is unpinned, the keyboard shortcut will not pin it. If another pinned editor becomes unpinned, then, with two editors unpinned, any editor can be pinned as normal. The cause seems to be the calculated state for the 'pinned' status of an editor. My keyboard shortcuts check those to determine wheter a keyboard shortcut should pin or unpin the editor. When I use the VSCode state inspection tool, I see that a pinned editor has a state of 'unpinned'. title: add accessibility signal for speech to text in progress
body:
We have a great visual indicator now when a speech to text session is in progress as demoed here https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-speech. Placeholder text appears with [INLINE_CODE] and the microphone icon is illuminated when the session is in progress.

We should indicate this to screen reader users as well with an audio cue / alert on progress start / stop.

similar_issues.text: refine when accessibility signals play in code editor. type : < b > bug < / b > i'm grouping together in this single issue several issues related to audio cues and accessibility - related text notifications in the editor. this is because they appear to be closely related and likely share a common cause. it is suspected that the triggering mechanism for both the audio cue and the text alert is the same, leading to the observed problematic behavior. in the visual studio code editor, there are issues related to the audio cues that have been present in previous versions. additionally, with the introduction of accessibility - related text notifications in v1. 86, new problems have arisen. these notifications, intended for screen reader users, are triggered when the cursor encounters lines with errors, warnings, breakpoints, etc. the issues with these features are as follows : 1. both the audio cues and accessibility - related text notifications are triggered whenever the cursor moves within the line, such as when using control + left / right to navigate to the previous / next word. this is particularly disruptive for the text notifications, as the repeated reading of the word " error ", " warning ", etc., often interrupts the normal verbalization of the screen reader. it would be more effective if these cues and notifications were only triggered when moving to a different line. 2. there appears to be a slight delay before the accessibility - related notification is announced. if the user moves too quickly between lines, the notification is not read in sync with the corresponding line, or sometimes it is read multiple times. it would be more efficient if the notification for a line was cancelled when the user moves to another line, ensuring it is always synchronized with the appropriate line. an advanced approach could be to have different audio cues for line - specific errors / warnings / breakpoints and " inline " errors / warnings / breakpoints. one suggestion would be to use the same sound but with different pitches for these two types of cues. this would not be necessary for certain audio cues that are only line - specific ( such as folded code ) or triggered by specific events ( such as task audio cues ). vs code version : code 1. 86. 0 ( 05047486b6df5eb8d44b2ecd70ea3bdf775fd937, 2024 - 01 - 31t10 : 28 : 19. 990z ) os version : windows _ nt x64 10. 0.

test: persistent progress part in chat. - [ x ] anyos @ sbatten - [ x ] anyos @ alexr00 complexity : 1 [ create issue ] ( https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode / issues / new? template = blank & body = testing + % 23311259 % 0a % 0a & assignees = justschen ) - - - this iteration, to show more consistency in how progress is rendered in chat, we are introducing a version of working progress that is basically [ inline _ code ] shown. down the line, this can be used to track token count and time spent as well potentially. # # testing : 1. make sure that [ inline _ code ] is enabled. this is currently enabled by default in insiders, and will go out in experimentation for stable. 2. observe that pretty much 100 % of the time now there will be some kind of consistent progress that is shown! 3. try doing things that require confirmation and note that the persistent confirmation won't show the working spinner anymore. 4. by default, if you have [ inline _ code ] empty, there should be an array of rotating messages. 5. disabled [ inline _ code ] and note that the experience should go back to normal. # # things to look out for : - weird rendering issues, particularly if there are multiple things rendering some kind of progress at the same time - jumping or weird stuttering

Test: Markdown extension. parent : https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode - internalbacklog / issues / 7919 # # goal choose the architecture for spoken agent responses in a hands - free voice session : existing extension - provided tts, realtime backend - streamed audio, or a capability - negotiated mix. # # current baseline vs code can synthesize chat response chunks through [ inline _ code ], and [ inline _ code ] provides a local / native aria tts model through [ inline _ code ]. voice code receives [ inline _ code ] chunks from its realtime backend and coordinates playback with barge - in suppression, session ids, and assistant transcript text. # # proposed work - compare client - side [ inline _ code ] tts latency, quality, interruption behavior, and offline support against backend - streamed audio. - determine whether backend audio is required for conversational timing, turn - taking, or model - selected spoken summaries. - define provider capabilities needed for streaming, cancellation, progress events, and barge - in. - decide how generated spoken text is captured for transcript / prior - timeline recall. - preserve the existing [ inline _ code ] and [ inline _ code ] behavior. - document privacy, policy, and data - flow implications for server - side audio generation. # # non - goals - do not remove the existing tts provider path. - do not require backend audio before state - driven narration can be prototyped. - do not read raw code - heavy output aloud unless explicitly requested by the user. # # open questions - should the speech provider api grow explicit streaming / cancellation capabilities, or should realtime audio live in a chat / agent voice layer? - how should barge - in interact with existing text - to - speech sessions? - which architecture gives the best behavior for web, desktop, remote, and offline scenarios?

[Accessibility]: Make syntax highlight accessible to screen reader users via a speech scheme. cc @ meganrogge and @ isidorn syntax highlight remains inaccessible to screen reader users. i propose using a speech scheme to address this issue. speech scheme is a technique using and switching between different speech synthesizer voices for visual formattings, such as colors, fonts, sizes, etc. just like sighted people see different colors for syntax types, screen readers would be able to hear different voice per syntax highlight type. as far as i know, there is no straight way to communicate with screen readers to force them to switch voices. however, the following solutions are available : 1. using [ inline _ code ] attribute. the html [ inline _ code ] attribute is recognized via screen readers and supported screen reader voice engines, such as jaws / nvda vocalizer and ios / mac osx can detect and automatically switch between different voices ( e. g., en - us, en - gb, etc. ) 2. using server - side voice engines as an option for syntax highlight. just like vscode liveshare extension, you can consider using api to send a server - side voice engines to control all the details. however, screen reader users need to suspend their screen reader speech while using this option that might be inconvenient. to come up with a more robust solution in the long run, however, i think vscode team needs to work with some popular screen reader vendors. # # system info version : 1. 79. 0 - insider ( system setup ) commit : 666396ddec7708df2b986dcc178863faaa67c14d date : 2023 - 06 - 05t11 : 30 : 50. 018z electron : 22. 5. 5 chromium : 108. 0. 5359. 215 node. js : 16. 17. 1 v8 : 10. 8. 168. 25 - electron. 0 os : windows _ nt x64 10. 0. 22621

title: Voice support in editor and input boxes
body:
Around the workbench, it would be nice to have a command / key binding which allows activating a direct speech to text experience. This would particularly be useful in input boxes and markdown documents. 

This exists already for the terminal as [INLINE_CODE].

cc @bpasero

similar_issues.text: [Accessibility] Support speech typing in terminal. type : < b > feature request < / b > cc @ meganrogge [ inline _ code ] currently supports copilot chat only. however, its speech - input feature can empower people with dis / abilities to improve their typing performance in other editor areas. i understand that the speech - typing is primarily trained for natural languages rather than programming syntax ; however, the natural speech typing in editor areas is still useful for writing comments, drafting markdown / plaintext documents, etc. in terminal, the natural language speech input can be used in conjunction with [ inline _ code ] tool so there is no reason to prevent users from voice - typing through this extension in terminal. extension version : 0. 3. 2023110115 vs code version : code - insiders 1. 85. 0 - insider ( eb56719ae7653bff54989385818ef39e1cd73d29, 2023 - 11 - 24t15 : 21 : 39. 004z ) os version : windows _ nt x64 10. 0. 22631 modes :
Support speech typing in editor and input fields. related https : / / github. com / microsoft / vscode / issues / 199128 cc @ bpasero

Dictation support for visual studio code. hi, i wish to lodge a request to have vs code updated so that it can accept dictation input. currently, if you try to dictate into vs code using software like dragon ( the industry standard ), nothing happens. this is important to fix for people like myself who have long term hand injuries and are trying to figure out ways to program by voice. people have managed programming by voice in these situations, but the solutions are difficult to develop and not pretty. to be clear, i'm not asking that you develop voice commands to input symbols by voice, only that the text boxes in vs code ( and / or visual studio ) can accept dictation input by dragon ( preferably with full'select - and - say'support ). voice programmers can take care of the rest. does it have to be dragon? not necessarily. it could be any local speech recognition engine with good accuracy ( i'd argue that the decade old windows voice recognition isn't quite there yet ) and the ability to write custom voice commands. while there are few people using such technologies today, it is a subject of interest to all programmers, because they may need it in the future. - jole
Add multi command support in key binding.. like... [ inline _ code ] or... [ inline _ code ]

Add a way to bind a keybinding for a command from the F1 list. i think we've discussed this, but we've never written it down. imho, it would be very helpful to have an alternative action next to each command in the f1 list ( similar how open to the side is an alternative action in the ctrl + p file list ) that when executed would bring up the keybindings editor with the action selected and will execute the " edit " action on that command. e. g. i use [ inline _ code ] and today i always run it from the f1 list because it is not bound. it would be nice to have an action that allows me to record a keybinding for it such that i can easily map it.

title: Requesting for an advancement in file modification testing
body: Type: Feature Request To the developer who may concern: Visual Studio Code gave me a good time when I was handling with codes. One of what I love is the file modification testing, for example, a white dot will appear at one end of the title of the page card. A good feature for the method is that when I stick to undo all my modification made to the file, the file will be examined to be unmodified with the white dot disappear. But I've recently found some problems about the file modification testing method. When I use the input software along with Windows 11 to input Chinese, my pinyin input will appear on the screen waiting for selecting the ideal Chinese words. But when I regret adding one Chinese word to an unmodified file and I simply use the backspace key to get the pinyin off my file, the file will be examined to be modified. Even if I press Ctrl+Z for dozens of times, the file will still be regarded as a modified one. My suggestion is to add some complementary methods to examine whether a file is modified. From my perspective, VS Code can introduce a feature where when an undo command is made in the situation where there seems to be no more space for an undo operation, the program will use some method like hashing to compare the file in the editor with the file in the disk. As a result, if they are compared to be the same, the white dot can be removed. Thanks for any devotion in improving the using experience of VS Code! title: Bump postcss from 8.5.6 to 8.5.12 in /extensions/copilot

Bumps [postcss](https://github.com/postcss/postcss) from 8.5.6 to 8.5.12.
Changelog

Sourced from postcss's changelog.

8.5.12

  • Fixed reading any file via user-generated CSS.
  • Added opts.unsafeMap to disable checks.

8.5.11

  • Fixed nested brackets parsing performance (by @​offset).

8.5.10

  • Fixed XSS via unescaped </style> in non-bundler cases (by @​TharVid).

8.5.9

  • Speed up source map encoding paring in case of the error.

8.5.8

  • Fixed Processor#version.

8.5.7

  • Improved source map annotation cleaning performance (by CodeAnt AI).
